alerts.title: TDF toxicity signs present
alerts.message: Guidelines list lower back pain and bone aches as presenting signs of TDF toxicity. Patient reports chronic lower back pain and heavy feeling in thighs, worsening over 4 months. TDF is a known cause. However, occupational strain from truck driving is a plausible non-drug cause. Serum phosphate is low (0.78 mmol/L), which can be associated with TDF-induced Fanconi syndrome. Trace proteinuria could be from hypertension or renal toxicity.

evidence.recommended_action: Do LFTs and RFTs as per guideline management for TDF toxicity signs.

alerts.title: Missing TDF renal monitoring
alerts.message: Guidelines recommend doing LFTs and RFTs if signs of TDF toxicity are present. Patient has symptoms (back pain) and low phosphate. Current plan lacks specific lab monitoring. Creatinine 112 umol/L is within normal limits but does not rule out tubular dysfunction. No baseline eGFR or trend analysis is provided.

evidence.recommended_action: Order LFTs and RFTs, including serum phosphate and urinalysis for protein quantification.

alerts.title: EFV-amlodipine interaction
alerts.message: Guidelines state efavirenz could potentially decrease amlodipine levels. Patient is on EFV and amlodipine, with sub-optimally controlled BP (146/94). No dose adjustment is required per guidelines, but therapeutic effect may be reduced. Patient also admits to missed doses.

evidence.recommended_action: Monitor blood pressure closely and reinforce adherence. Consider alternative antihypertensive if control remains poor.

alerts.title: EFV 600mg vs 400mg use
alerts.message: Guidelines recommend EFV 400 mg for fewer adverse events and it is virologically non-inferior to EFV 600mg. Patient is on a fixed-dose combination containing EFV; the dose is not specified but likely 600mg. Using EFV 400mg could reduce toxicity risk.

evidence.recommended_action: Consider switching to an EFV 400mg-based regimen if available and appropriate.
